findings.mechanism: The final current-access check runs before recordAccess acquires the workspace advisory lock. On PostgreSQL, another workspace mutation can hold ws:<workspaceId> after snapshot/blob preparation. preparedAccess can finish assertWorkspaceAccess, then block in recordAccess -> mutate at the workspace lock. During that wait, membership/role revocation can commit under the independent ws:<tenantId> lock, or a session/API-token revocation can commit. After the workspace lock becomes available, recordAccess appends and the route releases previously prepared data without checking the credential or role again. Thus the explicitly fresh authorization can become arbitrarily stale while access recording waits.
findings.evidence: Source trace: app.ts:809-811 joins assertWorkspaceAccess and recordAccess in one atomic block, but assertWorkspaceAccess performs only reads. VisuaService.mutate reads the workspace, awaits lock(`ws:${found.id}`), then runs the append callback. Store.atomic joins the current transaction; PostgreSQL starts plain BEGIN and only serializes the explicitly requested advisory key. AuthService.setRole/removeMember use ws:<tenantId>, not the workspace key. The existing auditor-http blob-gate tests revoke before final authorization starts, so their passing results do not cover revocation during the later access-record lock wait. Counterevidence/limit: SQLite transaction serialization prevents the same concurrent storage interleaving on one driver; this is a PostgreSQL source-derived schedule, not an executed PostgreSQL reproduction.
findings.recommendation: Acquire the workspace/access-record lock before the final current credential, canonical tenant/workspace, and capability check; keep the append in that same transaction and avoid a later lock wait after authorization. Check cancellation after lock acquisition as well. Add a PostgreSQL regression that holds the workspace lock after blob preparation, commits membership revocation while the response waits, releases the lock, and requires denial with no prepared record or response bytes.

findings.mechanism: selected is initialized from enabled frameworks only on mount, while framework checkboxes are recomputed from each new workspace summary. If another member disables a selected framework while the same workspace remains open, the live summary update removes that framework checkbox but leaves its ID in selected. Both preview and ZIP requests keep submitting the hidden ID. The server rejects it as no longer enabled, and editing any remaining checkbox cannot remove the invisible selection, leaving this panel unable to recover without a remount/page reload.
findings.evidence: AuditorPanel.tsx:27 filters current enabled frameworks; line 28 uses a one-time useState initializer. query() emits every selected ID at line 44, while the checkbox removal handler at line 78 can only remove a currently rendered framework ID. ReportsPage keys the component only by canonical workspace ID, so a same-workspace summary refresh preserves selected. events.ts invalidates the workspace summary on live activity/workspace updates; useWorkspace refetches that summary. export-snapshot.ts rejects every requested ID not in the current enabled assessable list. The e2e retry case covers a transient 503 and a different-workspace remount, not a same-workspace framework removal. This is a deterministic source trace; no browser rerender was executed.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile selected against the currently selectable framework IDs whenever availability changes, clear the old capture/receipt when effective scope changes, and ensure in-flight results cannot restore a capture for removed scope. Preserve valid user selections. Cover a same-workspace refresh that disables one selected framework and verify a remaining valid framework can still be previewed/downloaded.
